info.title: IYA STS Account API
info.description: The user portal's API: everything a person can see and do about their own account in this trust realm. The person is ALWAYS the access token's subject — no operation takes a username, an id or a DN naming whose account it is. A token is obtained by the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) as the public client `sts-user-portal`, with `resource` set to this API, and is DPoP-bound (RFC 9449): send it as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a `DPoP` proof carrying `ath`. It stops working when the sign-on session it was issued on ends. The few operations marked `x-access: link` take no token: they spend the single-use secret of an activation or reset link they carry.

portal.description: The authorization code flow with PKCE as a public client; every token DPoP-bound (RFC 9449).

get.summary: Who you are, this session, and how you sign in
get.description:
Your username, subject and directory entry's DN; when the sign-on session began, how it authenticated (amr, acr) and when it ends; every standard inetOrgPerson attribute your entry holds, from a fixed list (`directory`, null with no directory or no entry — then `session` carries what the sign-in said); a summary of your credentials (`mechanisms`); the language your entry holds with those offered (`language`); and the realm's custom attributes whose definition shows them on the portal, with your values and whether you may change them (`customAttributes`, empty with no entry).

The door of the portal's `GET /portal`.

post.description:
The credential named by its `id` is revoked. post.summary: Connects or disconnects a consumer provider
post.description:
`connect` answers `location`, the provider's authorization address: send the browser there. It needs a sign-on session whose risk is LOW or unscored, and an authentication within federation.connectRecentAuthMinutes — otherwise the answer is `stepUp`, a sign-in again. The answer sets the `sts_fed_link` cookie, which finishes the connect only in the browser holding it. `disconnect` removes your connection and ends the sessions it started; it is refused (409) while the connection is your only way to sign in — no password, passkey or other connection.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/connected-accounts`.

Takes no token: the link's `user` and `token` are the credential. Spends nothing — a link opened by a prefetch or a mail scanner still works. Rate limited. Every failure answers the same sentence. The answer is the first step: the password rules, whether a passkey and an authenticator app are offered, and whether a passkey may be the only way in (`passkeyAlone`, #1135).

post.summary: Answers one step of an activation
post.description:
`setup` sets the password and starts a passkey (the `key` view) or an authenticator app (the `totp` view) where they were chosen; `key` answers the passkey's ceremony; `totp` the app's code. The link is checked again, claimed before anything is set, and spent only by the step that finishes, which answers the `ready` view. Nobody is signed in by it. A passkey carries no role (#1135): `passkey` asks for one, and `key_role` is still accepted, `primary` and `mfa` both asking for one.

The door of the portal's `POST /portal/activate`.
